Welcome to Hook Infant School
We are delighted to welcome you to our wonderful school and to share with you what makes Hook Infant School such a special place for children to learn, thrive and flourish.
It is a privilege to join the Hook Infant School community, and I am excited to work alongside our children, families and staff as we continue to build on the school's many strengths.
Our vision and values underpin everything we do. We work together to provide a happy, secure and stimulating environment where children are motivated to learn, valued as individuals and encouraged to achieve their full potential. Through kindness, respect and a commitment to helping one another succeed, we aim to ensure that every child feels they belong, is inspired to explore and is supported to grow.
Children are at the heart of our school. We believe that every child should feel safe, respected and celebrated for who they are. Through strong relationships, a nurturing environment and high expectations for all, we help children develop confidence, curiosity, resilience and a lifelong love of learning.
The infant years are a precious and important time in a child's life. They provide the foundation upon which future learning, wellbeing and success are built. We are passionate about giving every child the very best start to their educational journey, ensuring they leave us with happy memories, strong friendships and the belief that they can achieve great things.
As a school at the heart of Hook village, partnership is incredibly important to us. We value the strong relationships we build with families and recognise that children achieve their best when school and home work together. Our dedicated staff, supportive governors, fantastic Hook Schools Community Association and strong links with Hook Junior School all contribute to the warm and welcoming atmosphere that visitors often comment upon.
I hope our website gives you a flavour of the warmth, ambition and sense of community that make Hook Infant School such a wonderful place to learn and grow. We are incredibly proud of our school and would be delighted to welcome you for a visit, where you can see our vision of every child belonging, exploring and growing in action.

Maths Vision Statement
Our Maths Vision Statement
‘Mathematics is a creative and highly inter-connected discipline that has been developed over centuries, providing the solution to some of history’s most intriguing problems. It is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment. A high-quality mathematics education therefore provides a foundation for understanding the world, the ability to reason mathematically, an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.’ National Curriculum 2014
At Hook Infant School, we teach a mastery approach to learning mathematics to ensure every child can achieve excellence in their fluency, understanding and knowledge. Teaching for mastery means children are able to know and understand mathematical concepts. It allows children to have a deep understanding of the subject through a concrete, pictorial and abstract approach and encourages them to make links in their knowledge to apply it to different concepts and problems. Therefore, children have a confident grasp of what they are learning and do not just remember to repeat routines without the ability to understand mathematical structures in order to make connections. To achieve this, we have created a curriculum in KS1 using the National Curriculum 2014 based around the Hampshire’s ‘I can…’ Learning Journeys, NCETM Teaching for Mastery materials, The White Rose resources, as well as drawing upon other useful aids such as Nrich tasks and I see reasoning questions. In the Early Years Foundation, we are following The White Rose documentation to deepen children’s knowledge and understanding, and this is in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum. Our learning journeys are aimed to build upon prior learning by breaking understanding into simple steps using models and images, practical resources, promoting mathematical vocabulary and solving problems by applying their mathematics to a variety of routine and non-routine questions. To improve mathematical fluency within our curriculum, EYFS and KS1 are following the NCETM mastering number programme which aims to strengthen the understanding of number and fluency with number facts, and develop a mathematical way of thinking for all children. We expect most children to move through the curriculum at broadly the same pace, with appropriate challenges at each stage encouraging problem solving and reasoning for all children. Those children that grasp mathematical concepts quickly will be given rich problems to extend their knowledge and understanding and will be encouraged to ‘Dive Deeper’ into mathematical concepts with more sophisticated reasoning. Children who are not sufficiently confident with early concepts of mathematics will be given additional practise and support to plug the gaps in their understanding before moving on.

pageCache.text:
Current Parents
Welcome to Year 1 and Curriculum Map
The Year 1 team work together to provide a stimulating learning environment that enables all the children to reach their full potential. Through developing an open and enquiring attitude to the world around them, Year 1 prepares its pupils for the opportunities, experiences and responsibilities for life in and around school. The children are encouraged to become as independent as possible and are invited to nominate their peers to become a School Council member to represent the views of all the children in our school.
Please have a look at our half termly curriculum map leaflets (downloads available on the right and sent home to you via parentmail) which outline what we are learning in school and how you can help your child continue with their learning at home.
Please also find the Introduction to Year 1 - Parent Talk below. Thank you for those who could attend the meeting and for those taking the time to read through the slides if not. Your support is greatly appreciated.
Miss Tamblin and The Year 1 Team

pageCache.pageTitle: Hook Infant School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Current Parents
Vision and Values
At Hook Infant School we work together as a community to provide a happy, secure and stimulating environment where children are motivated to learn, are valued as individuals and encouraged to achieve their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hook Infant School - Welcome to Year R
pageCache.text:
Current Parents
Welcome to Year R
“Every child deserves the best possible start in life and support to fulfil their potential. We aim to ensure a smooth transition into school life, promote positive attitudes, and develop self-confidence and independence.”
Hook Infant School EYFS Policy
We provide a programme of learning that has been devised for young children to develop in a happy, safe and caring environment. They learn through play in an interactive and exciting setting that encourages them to explore and make sense of their own surroundings; in both the indoor and outdoor areas - whatever the weather! Information on our current topic can be found on the main Reception page. All our activities follow the guidance of the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum.
The Year R Team are dedicated to ensuring that every child has the best possible start to their education. We are also aware that it can be an apprehensive time for their families too, so if you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Our Facebook Page (Hook Infant School) has ideas for ways you can support your child at home. Any resources linked to the Facebook page are on the website.
Thank you for all your continued support.

Wraparound: Koosa Kids Breakfast Club
Kick starting your children’s school day, every school morning.
KOOSA Kids operate Breakfast Clubs on behalf of Hook Infant School, as our wraparound care provider, every school morning.
The focus for our Breakfast Club is to provide a calm, welcoming and relaxing environment for your children ready for their busy day ahead.
A healthy and nutritious breakfast is served every morning (fruit, toast, cereals, fruit drinks, water) and the children are able to choose from a selection of quiet games and activities including art tables, board games, construction games, books and many more. Breakfast is on offer for the first 20 minutes of the session. At the end of the session, children are safely escorted to their classes.
Koosa Kids can be contacted directly by phoning 08450942322 or via their website www.koosakids.co.uk
